Shoji paper transmits roughly 40–50% of light. Matches figures quoted by shoji-paper retailers and paper-industry commentary (also 35–45% reflectance), but no manufacturer test standard or public-body source was found.
'30–40 cm of dead space above a closet rail or door' and '10–15 cm gap beside the fridge or washing machine' — plausible product-category ranges, no source.

Average rental flat for one person in Tokyo's 23 wards is about 25–30 m². 25 m² is the MLIT minimum housing standard for a single person and is the most common size in consumer surveys, but no official 23-ward average was located.
Standard oshiire depth 'about 80–90 cm'. Sources give 80–85 cm as standard interior depth; the upper end of the article's range is high.
Storage drawer units are sold in widths of 39, 44 and 54 cm. These are common retailer sizes (Nitori, Iris) but not a published standard.
'Many now do it in three stages as autumns lengthen.' Trend claim, no source.

'Many condominium rules ban futon over the rail.' True of many management bylaws but varies by building; the article already says to check.

“Heated Japanese rooms drop to 20–30% humidity” and “40–60% target” as a household target — the legal standard (Building Sanitation Law, unchanged in the Apr 2022 revision) is 40–70% RH for specified buildings; the 40–60% figure is convention, not a standard.
“Japanese homes swing from 80% humidity to 25% in a year” — no source found for these two endpoints as a national pattern; JMA data would be needed.
“many households moved to steam or hybrid types” after the pneumonitis reports — no shipment statistics found.
“It is one of the standard fall-prevention items on municipal checklists” — not verified against any specific municipal checklist.
Donation of ¥1,000–5,000 per household as the typical range — local convention, no published survey found.

“An estimated 300,000 festivals a year” — widely repeated estimate (about 81,000 shrines x ~3 festivals + temples + ~5,000 municipal events ≈ 310,000); no official statistic exists. The article already flags it as an estimate.
“Bon odori (July–August)” — many districts on the old lunar calendar (and Okinawa) hold it in September; range may need widening.
“¥30–60 per pad; a winter's daily use is ¥3,000–5,000” — bulk packs are often ¥15–30 per pad; Nikkei reports kairo prices up about 20% over five years, but no per-unit official figure found.
Kyusu capacity 200–360 mL, cups 80–150 mL, and hand-made kyusu price range — retail conventions, no authoritative source.
Source “Aichi Prefecture — Tokoname ware” points only at https://www.pref.aichi.jp/ (site root); a specific traditional-craft page was not located.
'Landlords expect tenants to re-mesh screens themselves' — no source; treatment of amido under 原状回復 guidelines not checked.
'Mosquito season runs May–October' as a nationwide statement; season length varies by region (Okinawa/Kyushu longer, Hokkaido shorter).
Mesh specification '18–24 mesh, grey or black polypropylene' and the claim that finer 24–30 mesh blocks some pollen — no manufacturer or public source located.
'PSE-marked but quality varies; NITE has reported charger incidents' — NITE alerts cover lithium-ion products and cheap non-genuine batteries generally, not 100-yen-shop chargers specifically.
'¥100 adhesive hooks hold 1–2 kg' and 'kitchen consumables come from the same factories as branded goods' — not verifiable.
'¥100 items are about 70% of the range' — no company or industry figure found; chains are publicly moving away from ¥100-only lines.
'A clogged filter drops airflow by half and is a fire risk in heater units (NITE reports)' — NITE bathroom heater-dryer incident data not reached.
'Mould grows above 70% humidity at 20–30°C' — commonly cited thresholds start nearer 60% RH with optimum growth at 25–30°C; the 70% figure is defensible but not from a primary source.
'Keep 20 cm+ clearance around the outdoor unit' — manufacturer clearances differ by model (front vs rear vs sides).
'Professional cleaning every 2–4 years' interval — a trade rule of thumb, no public-body source.
'A 2-person household pays ¥5,000–8,000 per two months' for Tokyo water and sewer — plausible but not checked against the Tokyo Waterworks Bureau tariff table.
'Fuel cost adjustment ±¥0–5/kWh' as the current band — TEPCO publishes this monthly and the September 2026 value was not confirmed.
'Total for a 2-person flat: 250–350 kWh/month, ¥8,000–12,000' — not checked against a survey statistic.
